decisions.contract: enforceContextWindow receives a numeric pendingTokens, not pending contents. Rank only committed rows here; preserve immediate per-replacement projection/reset and the first replacement even if projection already fits. Do not substitute provider one-pass maximum-saving policy. Provider-source pending overlay remains the existing typed path.
decisions.publication: Native ordinal/label facts and held version drive the shared publisher; scalar path uses derived publication to preserve old context ranges, source path retains density replacement. Metadata-only mirrors let copyMetadata initialize its group, never weakening the empty-edit invariant.
decisions.tokens: Use the same single-tool-block wrapper and actual tokenizer as before. Pending scalar/completion budget, floating limit, tie order, incomplete/error status and fixed token boundaries are preserved. No zero count or partial floor workaround. sourceTokenCount input metadata is not involved in this scalar API.
decisions.tail: Existing source-stage overlay passes 512/8192 persisted rows with two pending units and 40 rows with 64/65/5000 pending units. Latest tie and changed-tail winner are asserted; warm changed tail decodes zero persisted response blocks. Current pending inputs remain outside durable history. This is stage-level, not another whole public ChatSession proof.
decisions.cost: Existing core 40/4000 cold fill and selected/warm-query cache/read experiments pass with the original 65536-byte cap and zero growth on history-only ready repeats. Overlay fills still remeasure pending input and write journal facts; no zero-byte overlay reuse or arbitrary pending capacity is claimed. Tail test candidate reconstruction makes two whole-history passes, not one per pending unit. Scalar repeated replacements structurally refill ranking and can trigger compaction.
decisions.lifetime: Actual sink samples at 512/8192 observe peak one converted row, final zero, with original bound two. Rank peaks 10/14 against 64. These are object lifetime results, not whole-heap/cache/pin capacity.
decisions.failures: Token/query/row65/abort exact causes and ordered cleanup pass; failed admission permits same-writer continuation. Existing #3919 original tests and groupWriter physical poison remain unchanged. No new fallback-specific physical write fault is claimed.
decisions.remaining: Unpinned 8192 compaction-file RED; structural rank maintenance and accounting; pending/stale capacity and aggregate heap/cache/pins; native-capable explicit disk APIs and absent-policy density; public ProviderNormalizationDisk; Phase6 request/body/key/message/tokenizer spools and guards; Phase8 shared reservations; full format/range/tail/cache/image/semantic generations, LENS/live bytes; W23/W25/cutover/cold Mistral and Phase9. Defaults unchanged.

coverageLimits.committedParity: Independent array and explicit-old disk comparisons check two replacements, floating limit, exact history/tokens/context ranges/durable rows at 3/64/65/512/5000. The 8192 case is retained enabled and RED when compaction creation is denied; it does not reach full parity comparison.
coverageLimits.pendingTail: 512/8192 persisted rows with fixed two pending units; separately 40 persisted rows with 64/65/5000 pending units. No full cross-product or independently old-array-expected tail-shadow matrix is claimed.
coverageLimits.shadow: Existing tool-ranking-native first case supplies the same response rows as both committed and pending, asserts two pending replacements, exact projection 4200 and no durable history stubs. It is not a complete independent shadow-history value/token/range/durable matrix.
coverageLimits.cancellation: Native pre-abort, measurement/query/admission identity and cleanup ordering are covered by accepted native failures. Do not infer native in-flight timer-abort coverage at every size.
coverageLimits.hasPendingRows: Scalar enforceContextWindow API receives a pending token count, not contents; this increment does not change candidate publication flags or promise full public ChatSession send coverage.
